sections.title: An algebraic quantization of gravity from the null cone
sections.abstract: The author develops a background-independent quantization of four-dimensional Lorentzian vacuum general relativity on intersecting null cones, reporting finite causal-diamond state spaces, black-hole entropy corrections, and one-loop semiclassical equations.
sections.claimed_result: The author's abstract claims a nonperturbative null-cone quantization with absolutely convergent intermediate-state sums, a finite-dimensional Hilbert space for a macroscopic causal diamond, the Bekenstein–Hawking entropy and its logarithmic correction for marginally trapped surfaces, and one-loop semiclassical Einstein equations.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Vacuum general relativity on four-dimensional Lorentzian spacetimes, using intersecting null cones and the author's specified algebra of observables and boundary states.
sections.unique_caveat: These are model-dependent preprint claims; the derivation and physical interpretation of the entropy and finite-state conclusions have not been independently assessed here.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: One Hacker News story had 265 points and 119 comments at the snapshot; the paper is cross-listed in mathematical physics. It was the only recovered mathematical candidate with a direct HF/HN attention match.

sections.title: The Transverse Finiteness Conjecture for pseudo-Anosov flows via universal circles
sections.abstract: The authors prove Mosher's conjecture that a taut finite-depth foliation of an atoroidal 3-manifold is almost transverse, up to orbit equivalence, to only finitely many pseudo-Anosov flows.
sections.claimed_result: The abstract and introduction state that universal circles yield finiteness up to orbit equivalence; for a finite-depth foliation almost transverse to a pseudo-Anosov flow without perfect fits, that flow is unique up to orbit equivalence.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The finiteness theorem assumes a closed, oriented, atoroidal 3-manifold and a taut finite-depth foliation; uniqueness additionally assumes a flow without perfect fits.
sections.unique_caveat: The theorem does not cover arbitrary 3-manifolds or foliations of unrestricted depth; the universal-circle argument depends on the stated hypotheses.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: No HF upvote or HN story matched this paper in the recovered batch. It is selected for resolving a conjecture posed in 1996 and for a second rigidity result linking geometric topology and dynamical systems.

sections.title: Reflection subgroups and the Lookup Conjecture
sections.abstract: The authors prove the Bruhat-graph Lookup Conjecture for rational smoothness of Schubert varieties, its affine type-A extension, and a parabolic version for the type-A affine Grassmannian.
sections.claimed_result: The authors' abstract states that they prove the original Lookup Conjecture and its extension to affine type A~n; the introduction gives a degree-monotonicity criterion for parabolic Bruhat graphs in the type-A affine Grassmannian.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The original statement concerns Schubert varieties for complex reductive groups; the extension is for affine Kac–Moody type A~n, with the parabolic result specialized to the type-A affine Grassmannian.
sections.unique_caveat: The paper says broader Kac–Moody applications require checking rank-three reflection subgroups; the affine extension established here is type A~n.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: No HF/HN attention match was found. The placement reflects two conjecture-level results and a parabolic strengthening, with cross-listing across combinatorics, algebraic geometry, and representation theory.

sections.title: A proof of the Nevo-Peeva conjecture: Exact regularity and linear powers of gap-free edge ideals
sections.abstract: For every finite simple gap-free graph and every field, the author proves an exact formula for the regularity of every ordinary power of its edge ideal, resolving two conjectured properties of those powers.
sections.claimed_result: The abstract claims reg I(G)^q = max{2q, reg I(G)+q−1} for all q ≥ 1 when G is gap-free, yielding the exact linear-resolution threshold and the proposed regularity recurrence.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: G is a finite simple graph with at least one edge, I(G) its edge ideal over a field K, and the formula assumes G is gap-free.
sections.unique_caveat: The theorem is restricted to gap-free graphs; it is not a formula for powers of edge ideals of arbitrary graphs.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: No HF/HN attention match was found. The result resolves both Nevo–Peeva questions in the stated graph class and bridges commutative algebra with graph combinatorics.

sections.title: The asymptotic spectrum of tensors is connected
sections.abstract: For complex tensors of every fixed order k ≥ 3, the authors prove path-connectedness of the asymptotic spectrum and conclude that its values at any fixed tensor form a closed interval.
sections.claimed_result: The abstract claims every spectral point connects by a path to a one-leg-versus-rest flattening rank, making the asymptotic spectrum at a fixed tensor a closed interval and answering Strassen's question.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The main theorem concerns complex tensors of fixed order k ≥ 3; the broader interpolation method applies to Strassen semirings satisfying the paper's decomposability and cover-property conditions.
sections.unique_caveat: The wider method is conditional on those structural properties; the abstract does not assert that every asymptotic problem or semiring satisfies them.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: No HF/HN attention match was found. The authors answer a question of Strassen and give an interpolation method with stated applications beyond tensors; the mathematical contribution is cross-listed with representation theory.
